notes.title: Surgeon Simulator 9th Anniversary Retrospective
notes.content:
Hi surgeons!

Can you believe it's been 9 years since the original Surgeon Simulator launched?! It's fair to say that the game was a defining moment in Bossa's history and helped shape us in to the studio we are today.

We're celebrating the games 9th Birthday by offering some hefty discounts across both the original Surgeon Simulator and Surgeon Simulator 2: Access All Areas, as well as a special Anniversary Bundle which includes both games at a heavily discounted price point! 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40357378/31bb7f54e4ed3edfe0452a48cbd597a4d7c3b5ed.png

------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

We also have a short retrospective about the original games development from lead game designer Luke Williams to share with you, enjoy!

The theme of the 2013 Global Game Jam was the "sound of a heartbeat" but what outside influences (if any) inspired you to interpret that in the way that you did and come up with a surgery themed game?

I think our actual first thought was a heart transplant, something very literal involving a heart. We toyed around with a couple of other ideas after that because we felt it was a little on the nose, and not a very creative way of interpreting the theme, but ultimately we kept coming back to the heart transplant idea!

The original Surgeon Simulator prototype was made in just 48 hours, what do you think the biggest development challenge was with such a short window?

You never have as much time as you think you do. If you think you have a small idea, make it smaller, and then make it smaller again. The biggest challenge is always when you start trying to finalise the "game". Suddenly you're like "Oh we need a score, timers, main menu, completion screen..." and those things can really sneak up on you.

Were there any features that you would have liked to have included in that original prototype that eventually made it in to the full game?

Nothing major actually, one thing we thought we could do was add more to completing a surgery. In the game jam we originally wanted you to have to attach the new organ but we ran out of time and couldn't think of a good mechanic for it so we just went with "just slap it in the right sort of position and call it a day...". When it came to the full game that vague completion criteria actually drove a lot of the setting and narrative so we ended up leaving it how it was and focus on different organs and areas of the body. 

As mentioned, the original prototype was made in just 48 hours and then the full version of Surgeon Simulator was made in just 48 days. Was it a conscience decision to restrict development time of the full game to 48 days to keep in-theme with the original 48 hours, or was just purely coincidental?

Hah it was neither. As we were getting closer to launch I think we looked at the development and it was close to 48 days so we stretched the truth a little and said that it was, just because it sounded nice for the trailer. I'm sorry to anyone who feels betrayed by this revelation.

What did you find most challenging about scaling the prototype experience up into a full game?

For me it was certainly a "now what?" moment. It wasn't immediately obvious what areas to expand into a full game. Early on we figured we could do a kidney transplant but after that humans don't really have much more to dig around in their torso for. The possibilities really opened up when one of our IT guys suggested trying to do surgery in the back of a moving ambulance, it was a bit of a lightning strike moment and we instantly knew we had to do it. We still had to keep the scope small but extra environments allowed us to put twists on the already existing surgeries and mixed up the gameplay and chaos enough to warrant us calling it a full release!

The controls in Surgeon Simulator are legendary by this point but also very divisive - did you ever consider taking the "simulation" aspect a little more seriously and making the controls a little less "slapstick"?

Nope, never came into question haha. We had a few people in the company coming to us and saying "We literally can't select the first level" but we were young and stubborn and decided that would be the defining aspect of the game. Though I will clarify that while the controls are very difficult, they are consistent. We tried very hard to make sure the controls only did what you told them. This is what lead to many players persevering and having 1 more go, because ultimately each attempt you would do a little better!

Finally, looking back is there anything that you would have done differently with either the original game jam prototype or the full version of Surgeon Simulator 2013?

We had a location idea of doing surgery in the back of a plane in flight, complete with loops, barrel rolls and banking, that would've been wild. Essentially I would've loved to add more locations and other environmental challenges to interfere with your... attempts at surgery. Perhaps in a future game?....

So there you have it! We hope you'll join us in wishing the original Surgeon Simulator a happy 9th Birthday and we'd love to hear what your favourite memory from the Surgeon Simulator franchise is, so drop us a comment and let us know!

notes.title: DOCTOR’S NOTES: VERSION 1.5
notes.content:
A belated Happy New Year, surgeons! Since returning back to the studio, the Surgeon Simulator 2 team have been focused on squashing bugs and making general game improvements, and we have a new version of Surgeon Simulator 2: Access All Areas ready for all our PC players. 

Update Surgeon Simulator 2: Access All Areas to version 1.5 on PC to gain access to the following patches:

 Level ratings now correctly appear on the thumbnails in the terminal, so you can easily see which is a highly rated level!
 General UI improvements, such as ensuring appropriate buttons are highlighted. 
 Newly created and validated levels can now be seen in the ‘Newest Levels’ list in the terminal. 
 Fixes for the terminal displaying as blank when loading into the lobby. 
 We’ve given Bob his blood back in the Surgery 101 level… where did it even disappear to!?
 SFX fixes in Creation Mode.
 Improvements for controller on PC, including a fix for loss of controller functionality when viewing Community-Made Levels in the terminal, and the ability to ‘favourite’ and ‘unfavourite’ levels using controller input. 
 Winning players will now (rightfully!) be displayed on the end of the level screen in Campaign Levels. 
 Thumbnails for Community-Made Levels levels now appear, rather than being stuck in a loading state.
 Levels no longer appear as ‘invalid’ when players create a custom queue. 
 Sometimes the vactubes get a bit blocked, and now all players will receive a ‘Tubes Jammed’ prompt should an issue occur. 
 Backend improvements to speed up the client. 

If you encounter anything that doesn’t seem right in-game, remember you can always submit a ticket to our customer service team here. Happy surgery-ing! 2022 is the year you’ll get your medical licence, we can feel it.

notes.title: What’s New in the Surgery Room?
notes.content:
Hello surgeons!

It’s been almost two months since we launched Surgeon Simulator 2: Access All Areas on Steam and we have been working hard to fix issues and deliver a great Halloween update (which is now live!), so we would like to give you a quick update of what else has changed since launch.

Apart from several small fixes and some quality of life improvements, here is a list of the things we have fixed and changed so far thanks to your feedback:


 We've listened to your feedback and will no longer automatically add friends to your Steam friends list when adding them in the game. Be aware that removing a friend from your Steam friends list will also remove them from your in-game friends list
 Fixed player names displaying incorrectly at the end of a level
 Adding a friend in Steam now adds the friend in-game. Removing a friend needs to happen both in-game and in your Steam friends list, for full flexibility


We would also like to mention that the long loading screens and authentication issues should also have improved - we have made some important server side updates that hopefully helped.

We really hope that these fixes made a great impact in your experience and you can focus on the most important matter: performing terrible surgeries with your friends. 

Please keep sending us your feedback! Your bug reporting and support messages mean a lot to us.

Aside from that, we have a message from one of our lead developers on the title, Mark:

Safe to say it’s been a busy month since we launched on Steam! The team has been overwhelmed, in the best way, with the number of players jumping into the surgery and operating on Bob.

As with any live service game, there were a few teething issues. We have now pushed out fixes across all platforms to solve the most prominent problems, such as those stopping players from getting into the game altogether or joining in with friends. The team is continuing to work hard on terminating any existing bugs, and we can’t thank you enough for your patience and understanding.

Surgeon Simulator 2: Access All Areas has been a labour of love over the last few years, and it’d mean a lot to the team if you could leave a Steam review for the game. Steam reviews are super important for indie developers and publishers, and we love to read all your positive experiences. 

A big thank you, again, for giving Surgeon Simulator 2: Access All Areas a whirl. Between completing development and QA work, watching your live streams, seeing your ridiculous screenshots and reading about your fun in-game experiences is our favourite thing ✌️ 

If you want to keep up to date with all things Surgeon Simulator 2, please consider joining our Discord channel too!

notes.title: The "Trick and Treat" Update Has Arrived
notes.content:
It’s the season to be spooky! As if performing experimental surgeries with axes and saws isn’t horrifying enough, we’ve just released a brand new update to Surgeon Simulator 2: Access All Areas for players across all platforms.

Dubbed the Trick and Treat update (y’know, treat because you’re the ones treating Bob), you’ll be able to find a whole host of new Halloween content in-game. This includes multiplayer, spooky-themed levels created by our in-house level designers and a handful of talented community members: 


 Bobenstein 
 Of Trials and Traps 
 Halloween Games
 Giant Spider Boss
 The Mysterious House
 Moonlight Cave
 Room Service


All the above levels are multiplayer and can be found in the terminal. All levels also take advantage of the new Halloween props and textures which have arrived as part of the Trick and Treat update; with 18 new pieces available in the level creation tool. 

The new props and textures include cauldrons, witch legs, skeleton doggos, spiders, hanging corpses and ghosts, pumpkins, candles, tombstones and spooky trees. All the basics required to build a completely terrifying in-game level. 

On top of new levels, props and textures, we’ve also added a selection of Halloween costumes and masks. Browse through your Halloween fits using the mirror in the lobby, with new full-body costumes and eight Halloween masks.

https://labs.bossastudios.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/10/BOSSA-SSSP-35B.gif

The Trick and Treat update is completely free for everyone who owns Surgeon Simulator 2: Access All Areas, simply update your game and scrub-in for some spooky surgeries.

notes.title: Hotfix 1.3.7 Released
notes.content:
We've just pushed out hotfix 1.3.7 to make a minor change to the way the friends list functionality works.


 Adding a friend in Steam now adds the friend in-game. Removing a friend needs to happen both in-game and in your Steam friends list, for full flexibility.


Just for clarity, the friends list now works as follows:

Adding a friend in-game does not add the friend in Steam
Adding a friend in Steam does add the friend in-game
Removing a friend in-game does not remove the friend in Steam
Removing a friend in Steam does not remove the friend in-game

notes.title: Known Issues & What We’re Working On!
notes.content:
Surgeon Simulator 2: Access All Areas is a-live across Steam, Xbox, Xbox Game Pass, Epic Game Store and the Microsoft Store. Since launching on Thursday 2nd, we’ve seen thousands of aspiring surgeons jumping into the game to fix, or worsen, Bob’s ailments.

Launching a live game often comes with a few teething problems, and whilst we’ve seen plenty of funny streams, screenshots and videos of people enjoying Surgeon Simulator 2: Access All Areas, we’re also aware of some issues a portion of players are facing. 

We’ve logged all reported bugs and technical issues safely stored in our backlog but, for transparency, we wanted to list out the game issues that are being prioritised by the development team for the remainder of this week. These issues require a bit more work and attention than simply pushing out hotfixes, but here’s what we’re currently working on: 


Long loading screens, authentication issues, black screen issues

Most of these issues are related to our server capacity, which has been consistently overwhelmed since the game’s launch on Thursday due to high player demand. It’s our first Game Pass launch as a studio, and it’s been a learning curve for us. 

As soon as the server issues were identified, we began upscaling our capacity and are continuing to make improvements each day. Specific server improvements have been made to allow more players into the game, and we’re monitoring this on a regular basis.


Multiplayer issues, party disconnections and friends appearing offline

Surgery is best enjoyed with friends, but a portion of players aren’t actually able to team up with their friends to play Surgeon Simulator 2: Access All Areas. This is tied to the server issues mentioned above, but the developers are looking into multiplayer specific solutions to get this resolved across all platforms ASAP. 


Error pop-ups, voice / multiplayer ban messages

Don’t worry, we haven’t actually banned you. We’re aware of players across the Windows Store experiencing pop-up messages saying that they’re banned from multiplayer or communicating with other players. This is not the case and is in fact another known issue that we’re continuing to investigate.

Error messages cropping up during gameplay can usually be ignored, or dealt with by restarting the game, however as this has continued persisting it requires some developer time to get a solution. 


Progression problems, missing cosmetics
 
You may find that your game progress hasn’t been updated in-game, or that when you visit the mirror in the lobby you don’t have the right cosmetics or the cosmetics that you’re owed (for example, Plague Doctor). This issue is impacting a small number of players, but we’re looking into the progress reset issues as a matter of urgency. 

On top of reported bugs, there has also been plenty of community feedback, whether that’s around difficulties with controllers or general pieces of feedback. We have gathered all of this, and once we deal with the prioritised technical issues, we’ll move on to reviewing the feedback that’s been presented. 

If you’re experienced any of the above problems whilst trying to enjoy Surgeon Simulator 2: Access All Areas, we’re sorry, and we’re super grateful for your patience.

You can get more frequent updates on the official Discord server here.

notes.title: Modifier Madness!
notes.content:
Introducing a brand new feature for Surgeon Simulator: Access All Areas - Modifiers! Add a whole new level of difficulty (and fun!) to the game by turning on these whacky modifiers, which will provide endless hours of entertainment (and dare we say frustration?) for you and your friends! You can see some of the modifiers in action in our brand new trailer:

[previewyoutube=QcEJZeyaoZg;full][/previewyoutube]

And for a full breakdown of all the in-game modifiers and what they do, keep reading!

VISUAL DRUG EFFECT

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40357378/7ad611b01b6b87d70a2a6c838dfcbcc57cf8a7a4.png

Prepare to see a surgery of shapes and colours with this visual drug effect. 

It’s not recommended to complete surgery under the influence...

INPUT DRUG EFFECT

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40357378/c18ca1fc6e9adad70083aaa4279ef57ba88ae954.png

A different type of drug that helps you walk, erm... creatively.

Tried walking to the left? Expect to go right. This effect reverses and randomises your surgeon's input.

BUTTER FINGERS

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40357378/d083f08ecab2665953d57dee3e60b0bf996854b9.png

This is why it’s important to wash your hands!

Holding objects just got a lot more slippery, so prepare to be dropping things more than usual.

CRAB WALK

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40357378/663ddd68accf7c4f7f8d9c7de3a6ed2b5dc272fa.png

This effect will have your character stuck in the crouch position.

It really puts you in a pinch!

FLOPPY ARM

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40357378/6e099fb3c8461b23ad6812f54d03668336134026.png

What even are bones? 

Be prepared to face great difficulty straightening your arm and picking up tools with this effect.

LIGHTS OUT

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40357378/c77424afd078f2acbc5d5a3554fb740c55cfdd51.png

How’s your night vision? 

This effect plunges the level into darkness, with only a few glow sticks to guide you around - like the good old days!

SPAWN RANDOM SYRINGE

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40357378/5253ac7eb7d03ad263175766baf5e6694f308361.png

It’s raining syringes! This effect will spawn a red or yellow syringe for a random player.

Bossa Labs doesn't guarantee a 100% effectiveness, though...

SPAWN RANDOM TOOL

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40357378/f909f2ad5d0e7d0c72296394010441146a1c3a16.png

Will you get a saw, handsaw, hammer, scalpel or axe? There’s only one way to find out!

This effect will drop a random tool for each player… results may vary.

Finally, are you a Twitch streamer? Then embrace the mayhem even more and let your viewers decide your stream's fate by activating the fully compatible PC Twitch extension. Let your viewers vote which modifiers are activated during your session to make your operations as chaotic as possible.

So there you have it - a brand new feature coming to Surgeon Simulator 2: Access All Areas when it launches on Steam in one weeks time! We hope you all have as much fun with the modifiers as we've had [strike]playing[/strike], err... we mean testing them internally.

We'll see you in the OR and don't forget to add the game to your wishlist to help unlock those last couple of rewards!
